checks.title: A received message shows who it is from and who it went to, whatever RFC 5322 form the sender used
checks.gherkin:
Scenario: The senders and recipients of a received message are read in every form RFC 5322 allows
  Given mail has received the RFC 5322 Appendix A messages a1.1-sender, a1.2-mailboxes, a1.3-groups, a2-2-reply, a5-oddities, a6.1-obs-address and a6.3-obs-ws, byte-exact from the fixtures of research 01a19b44
  When mail reads each message
  Then its From, Sender, Reply-To, To, Cc and Bcc hold exactly the mailboxes and groups of that message's golden in body.goldens.read of research 01a19b44
  And a5-oddities reads From as Pete <pete@silly.test> and Cc as the group "Hidden recipients" with no members
  And a6.1-obs-address reads To as Mary Smith <mary@example.net> and jdoe@test.example, with the route and the empty element gone
  And a6.3-obs-ws reads From as John Doe <jdoe@machine.example>
  And none of these messages records a problem
proves: Mail SHALL read the address fields of a received message (From, Sender, Reply-To, To, Cc, Bcc) into mailboxes and groups as RFC 5322 3.4 and 4.4 define them
toy 01a18fb8: no existing parser reads A.5, A.6.1 and A.6.3; this is the check that mail's own reader does
goldens 01a19b44: readMessage reproduces the golden address fields of each fixture
intent proposals[3]: a mailbox that feels like the one people already use shows the right people on every message
checks.why_not_the_other_kind: Receiving a message and seeing its people is the one thing a user does here, and only readMessage over a whole message proves each of the six fields is read with the address reader.

checks.title: A display name is returned unquoted, its words joined as written; no name is null
checks.rule: A phrase's text joins its atoms, quoted strings and dots with one space before each spaced token, quoted strings lose their quotes and backslashes, and a mailbox with no phrase has name null.
proves: display names unquoted (RFC 5322 3.4)
A.1.2: "Joe Q. Public" and "Giant; \"Big\" Box" read as Joe Q. Public and Giant; "Big" Box; <boss@nil.test> has name null
checks.why_not_the_other_kind: Joining and unquoting tokens is a rule over a string; a user never does it, they see its result.

checks.title: Comments and folding white space inside an address are removed
checks.rule: Comments (nested, with quoted parentheses) and folding white space anywhere in a mailbox, local part, domain or group are dropped, so pete(his account)@silly.test(his host) reads as pete@silly.test and jdoe@test  . example as jdoe@test.example.
proves: comments and folding white space removed (RFC 5322 3.2.2, 4.4)
toy 01a18fb8: postal-mime read A.6.3 From as name 'John Doe . example', address jdoe@machine; this check fails that result
checks.why_not_the_other_kind: Dropping comments is a token rule with many small cases, which a unit test covers exhaustively and cheaply.

checks.title: An obsolete route before the addr-spec is dropped
checks.rule: In an angle address, an @ and everything up to the next colon is a route and is dropped, so <@node.test:mary@example.net> reads as mary@example.net.
proves: routes dropped (RFC 5322 4.4, obs-route)
toy 01a18fb8: postal-mime returned @node.test:mary@example.net as the address
checks.why_not_the_other_kind: The route is one grammar branch; a unit test isolates it from the rest of a message.

checks.title: Empty list elements are skipped, and an empty value is an empty list
checks.rule: Commas with nothing between them, in an address list or among a group's members, add no element, and an empty field value is an empty list.
proves: empty list elements skipped (RFC 5322 4.4, obs-addr-list, obs-group-list)
A.6.1: 'Mary Smith <@node.test:mary@example.net>, , jdoe@test  . example' reads as two mailboxes
checks.why_not_the_other_kind: List splitting is pure logic over tokens; no user action reaches it any differently.

checks.title: A group is kept with its members, an empty group with none
checks.rule: A phrase, a colon, mailboxes separated by commas and a closing semicolon read as one group named by the phrase holding those mailboxes in order; 'Undisclosed recipients:;' is a group with no members.
proves: groups kept with their members (RFC 5322 3.4)
A.1.3 and A.5: groups 'A Group' with three members, 'Undisclosed recipients' and 'Hidden recipients' with none
toy 01a18fb8: postal-mime added a member ')' to the empty A.5 group and a stray mailbox after A Group
checks.why_not_the_other_kind: The group grammar is a rule over tokens, best proved directly on its inputs.

checks.title: A quoted local part and a domain literal are returned as written
checks.rule: A local part keeps its quotes and a domain literal its brackets, so "john doe"@example.com and jdoe@[192.0.2.1] read with local '"john doe"' and domain '[192.0.2.1]'.
proves: mailboxes as RFC 5322 3.4.1 defines the addr-spec
a local part compares exactly: it can only if it is kept as written
checks.why_not_the_other_kind: Keeping the written form is a token rule; a user never sees it apart from the address it yields.

checks.title: A value that fits no address grammar reads as null, never as an invented address
checks.rule: readAddresses returns null when lexing fails (an unclosed comment, quoted string or literal) or any list element fits no mailbox or group, as with '<<<>>> ,,, @@@', 'lone@' and 'G: <bad;'.
proves: as RFC 5322 3.4 and 4.4 define them: what fits neither grammar is not a mailbox
toy 01a18fb8: postal-mime read the m6 garbage From as address '<' with name '>>' and reported no problem
checks.why_not_the_other_kind: Rejection is a property of the parser over many bad strings, which a unit test enumerates.

checks.title: Two mailboxes are the same when their domains match without ASCII case and their local parts match exactly
checks.rule: sameMailbox(a, b) is true when the domains are equal after folding A to Z only and the local parts are equal byte for byte, so Jdoe@Example.COM and Jdoe@example.com match, and jdoe@example.com and Jdoe@example.com do not.
proves: A domain compares without regard to case; a local part compares exactly (RFC 5322 3.4.1)
checks.why_not_the_other_kind: A comparison is a pure function of two values; no fixture or user action is needed to prove it.

failure_ways.way: readMessage does not pass one of the six fields (for example Reply-To or Bcc) through readAddresses, or passes the wrong field
failure_ways.caught_by: A received message shows who it is from and who it went to, whatever RFC 5322 form the sender used (Reply-To through a2-2-reply; Bcc only if a fixture carries it, see gaps)

failure_ways.way: A display name keeps its quotes or backslashes, or its words are joined with the wrong spacing
failure_ways.caught_by: A display name is returned unquoted, its words joined as written; no name is null

failure_ways.way: A mailbox with no display name gets an empty string or the address as its name
failure_ways.caught_by: A display name is returned unquoted, its words joined as written; no name is null

failure_ways.way: A comment or folding white space is left in the name, local part or domain, or a spaced dot splits the domain into a name
failure_ways.caught_by: Comments and folding white space inside an address are removed

failure_ways.way: A route is kept in the address
failure_ways.caught_by: An obsolete route before the addr-spec is dropped

failure_ways.way: An empty list element becomes an empty mailbox, or makes the whole field fail
failure_ways.caught_by: Empty list elements are skipped, and an empty value is an empty list

failure_ways.way: A group is flattened into its members, loses its name, or an empty group gets a member
failure_ways.caught_by: A group is kept with its members, an empty group with none

failure_ways.way: A quoted local part loses its quotes or a domain literal its brackets, so two different addresses read the same
failure_ways.caught_by: A quoted local part and a domain literal are returned as written

failure_ways.way: Garbage in an address field is read as a mailbox instead of null
failure_ways.caught_by: A value that fits no address grammar reads as null, never as an invented address

failure_ways.way: Domains compare with case, or local parts compare without case, or non-ASCII letters are folded
failure_ways.caught_by: Two mailboxes are the same when their domains match without ASCII case and their local parts match exactly

failure_ways.way: The reader lowercases the domain it returns, so the address is no longer as written
failure_ways.caught_by: A received message shows who it is from and who it went to, whatever RFC 5322 form the sender used (goldens hold domains as written); no fixture has an uppercase domain, see gaps

failure_ways.way: An address field that reads as null records no unparsed-value problem
failure_ways.caught_by: No SHALL of FR-MAIL-004 breaks: recording problems is the reading form's 'reports, never mends' rule, owned by the requirement for problems

gaps.question: No fixture in research 01a19b44 carries a Bcc field, so nothing proves Bcc is read. Should a Bcc line be added to a fixture (and its golden), or is Bcc on received mail accepted as unproven?

gaps.failure_way: The reader lowercases the domain it returns
gaps.question: No fixture has a mixed-case domain, so the goldens cannot catch a reader that folds case. Should one fixture carry an uppercase domain so 'returned as written' is proved end to end?

gaps.failure_way: A display name written as RFC 2047 encoded words shows as =?utf-8?...?= in the mailbox
gaps.question: FR-MAIL-004 says display names are unquoted but not whether encoded words in them are decoded, and the form keeps Subject as written. Does reading leave encoded words in names to the client, or does another requirement decode them?

gaps.failure_way: A group in From or Sender, or two Senders, is read as valid
gaps.question: The form reads From as mailboxes only and Sender as exactly one (RFC 5322 3.6.2), but FR-MAIL-004 neither states nor traces 3.6.2. Which requirement owns that rule, so its check is written there?

left_out.candidate: A unit test of the lexer alone for comments, quoted strings and literals
left_out.why: Rule 3: the lexer is shared by message-ids and dates and its rules are not this requirement's SHALL; this requirement's comment and white-space clause is proved through readAddresses.

left_out.candidate: One behaviour scenario per address field (From, To, Cc, and so on)
left_out.why: Rule 2: the user does one thing, receiving and reading a message, so the fields go in one scenario.

left_out.candidate: One behaviour scenario per Appendix A message
left_out.why: Rule 2: these are inputs to the same user action, not separate actions; the obsolete forms are proved by the unit tests and wired by the one scenario.

left_out.candidate: A behaviour scenario that IMAP ENVELOPE shows the addresses
left_out.why: Rule 3: the form hands ENVELOPE to IMAP, whose own requirement proves it.

left_out.candidate: Checks that a null address field records unparsed-value in readMessage's problems
left_out.why: Rule 3: problem recording is not a clause of FR-MAIL-004; it belongs to the requirement for problems.

left_out.candidate: A check that From must be mailboxes and Sender exactly one
left_out.why: Rule 3: RFC 5322 3.6.2 is not in this requirement's statement or traces; raised as a gap instead.

left_out.candidate: A comparison of address reading with postal-mime or Python email
left_out.why: Rule 3: toy 01a18fb8 already decided build over depend; the goldens are the oracle.
Rule 3: no corpus exists (01a19b44 and 01a19b46 mark it unverified); it is a research step, not a check of this SHALL.

left_out.candidate: A unit test that canonicalLocal is never used in reading
left_out.why: Rule 3: the sameMailbox unit test already fails if local parts are folded; a test of an absence adds nothing.
